sections.h2: What are the main ways to sell a house fast in Hollywood, FL?
sections.html:
Hollywood sellers usually choose between three routes: a traditional listing, a cash sale to an investor or buyer, or a sale to a company that buys as-is. The right pick depends on how much repair work the house needs, how soon you must close, and whether a lender or court deadline is driving the timeline.

A listing can bring the widest buyer pool, but it brings showings, inspections and financing contingencies too. A cash sale trades some of that exposure for speed and fewer conditions. Whichever route you take, the deed still has to be signed, witnessed, taxed and recorded in Broward County, and those steps look the same for every buyer.

  • Listing with an agent: more exposure, longer timeline, buyer's lender and appraisal involved.
  • Cash buyer or as-is purchase: fewer contingencies, shorter closing window, you skip repair work.
  • Selling to a relative or through a lease option: possible, but the deed tax and homestead rules below still apply.

sections.h2: What makes Hollywood a distinct place to sell a house?
sections.html:
Hollywood sits in southeastern Broward County between Miami and Fort Lauderdale, and the city describes itself as roughly 30 square miles and Broward's third-largest municipality. The Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 157,019 residents, up from 153,067 counted in 2020.

Joseph Wesley Young founded the city, and it was incorporated by charter on November 28, 1925. His plan laid out circles along a central boulevard, and Young Circle, now home to the ArtsPark, still anchors downtown. The September 1926 hurricane stopped the first building boom abruptly, and the city's own history records that population fell from about 18,000 to about 2,500 afterward. That record is a useful reminder that coastal Broward real estate has always moved with storms and credit cycles.

The housing stock is mixed. Census figures for 2020 to 2024 show a 58.9 percent owner-occupied rate, a median owner-occupied home value of $410,600 and median gross rent of $1,653. Renters make up a large share of households, so many Hollywood sellers are landlords rather than owner-occupants, which changes both the tax picture and the closing steps.

sections.h2: Which Hollywood neighborhoods and employers shape buyer demand?
sections.html:
Buyers look at three broad areas: the barrier-island strip along the Atlantic, historic downtown around Harrison Street and Young Circle, and the western Hollywood Hills section that grew after Hollywood Boulevard was extended toward U.S. 27 in 1954.

  • Beach: the Hollywood Broadwalk runs nearly 2.5 miles along the ocean, with condos and boutique inns on the oceanfront side.
  • Downtown: an arts and dining district centered on the ArtsPark at Young Circle.
  • Jobs nearby: about 80 percent of Port Everglades lies inside the city, Fort Lauderdale/Hollywood International Airport abuts it, and Memorial Regional Hospital and Joe DiMaggio Children's Hospital are major employers.

Census data shows a mean commute of 29.4 minutes, and the city lists I-95, the Florida Turnpike and Tri-County Commuter Rail among its transport links. Public schools in Hollywood are run by the School Board of Broward County, and the city counts more than 30 public and charter schools within its limits.

sections.h2: How does the homestead exemption affect a Hollywood sale?
sections.html:
If you live in the house, the homestead exemption ends with the sale, and the buyer starts fresh. Broward County's property appraiser explains that a seller's exemptions do not carry past the year of sale and that each new owner must apply on their own.

The state caps yearly assessed-value growth on a homestead at the lower of 3 percent or the change in the consumer price index, and a change of ownership resets the property to just value the following January 1. For a seller, the practical point is that the buyer's first tax bill may be higher than yours was. Buyers know this, so expect it to come up in negotiation.

If you are moving within Florida, ask the Broward property appraiser about portability. It lets you carry part of your Save Our Homes savings to a new homestead if you establish it within the window the state allows. The appraiser's page notes that portability needs a homestead application filed first, with a March 1 filing deadline for each tax year. For tax year 2027 the late-filing cutoff the appraiser prints is September 20, 2027.

Landlords should note that renting the property can end homestead eligibility. The appraiser's page lists renting out the home among the changes you must report, and back taxes can reach ten years with a 50 percent penalty and 15 percent interest.

sections.h2: What taxes and fees come with transferring a Hollywood house?
sections.html:
The main transfer cost is Florida's documentary stamp tax on the deed. The statute sets it at 70 cents on each $100 of consideration, and the Department of Revenue says all parties to the document are liable no matter who agrees to pay it. In practice the purchase contract decides who pays,.

Consideration includes money, discharge of an obligation, and any mortgage or encumbrance on the property, whether or not the buyer assumes it. So a sale with a payoff attached is measured on more than the cash that changes hands.

The clerk of the circuit court records the deed and collects the tax at recording. The recording charges in section 28.24 of the statutes are $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for each additional page, plus a $1.00 trust-fund charge on the first page and $0.50 on additional pages, plus a $4 per page technology charge. Ask the Broward County Records office or your closing agent for the exact total on your deed.

Property tax is handled separately. Taxes are assessed as of January 1, bills go out in November, and the state's discount runs 4 percent for November payment, 3 percent for December, 2 percent for January and 1 percent for February. Unpaid taxes turn delinquent on April 1. Your closing agent prorates the year between you and the buyer.

sections.h2: What if my Hollywood house is in foreclosure, probate or has tenants?
sections.html:
Each situation has its own clock, and each can still end in a sale. Get the paperwork in front of a Florida attorney early, because the dates are set by court order or statute.

  • Foreclosure: after a final judgment, the clerk sells the property at public sale at least 20 and at most 35 days later unless the plaintiff agrees to more time. A high bidder posts a 5 percent deposit, and objections are due within 10 days of the certificate of sale. Selling before the sale date can keep that process from running its course.
  • Probate: summary administration is available when the non-exempt estate is $150,000 or less, or when the decedent has been dead more than two years. Creditor claims are barred unless filed by the later of three months after first publication of the notice to creditors or 30 days after service on a known creditor.
  • Tenants: a month-to-month tenancy ends on at least 30 days' notice, and nonpayment starts with a three-day written notice that excludes weekends and court holidays. A buyer who wants vacant possession will ask where this stands.

Florida has no state estate tax. The Department of Revenue says personal representatives need not file Form DR-312 or DR-313 for deaths after 2004, and filing is no longer required as of July 1, 2023.

sections.h2: What should I gather before asking for a cash offer in Hollywood?
sections.html:
Having documents ready shortens the timeline more than anything else you control.

  • The recorded deed and the last tax bill (the tax collector can reissue it).
  • A payoff letter from each lender, and any HOA or condo estoppel request for association properties.
  • Lease copies and tenant contact details if the house is occupied.
  • A list of known repairs, open permits and storm damage claims.
  • For an estate sale, the letters of administration or the order from the probate court.

Florida law requires a conveyance of land to be in writing and signed in front of two subscribing witnesses. Plan your signing so those witnesses are present, or use the audio-video witnessing the statute allows.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Hollywood house without making repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. Cash buyers and as-is purchasers often take a house in its current condition, and you simply price that in. A listing sale can also close as-is, but a buyer's lender or inspector may still ask for repairs before closing.

faqs.q: Who pays the deed tax when a Hollywood house sells?
faqs.a: The contract decides who pays, but the Department of Revenue says every party to the deed is liable for the 70 cents per $100 rate regardless of the agreement. Check the purchase agreement and ask your closing agent to confirm the line item.

faqs.q: Does my homestead exemption move to the buyer?
faqs.a: No. Broward's property appraiser states that a seller's exemptions do not carry over beyond the year of sale, and each owner must apply. Ownership change also resets the assessed value to just value for the following January 1.

faqs.q: What if I owe back property taxes on a Hollywood house?
faqs.a: They are paid from the proceeds at closing, and the title agent will request a payoff figure. Taxes turn delinquent on April 1, and certificates can be sold by June 1, so contact the Broward tax collector for the amount due on your parcel.

faqs.q: How fast can a sale close in Hollywood?
faqs.a: It depends on the buyer, title work and any liens. Cash sales skip lender underwriting, which removes the longest step, but title search, payoff letters and deed recording still take time. Ask your buyer and closing agent for a written timeline.
